title: Pese a que + subjuntivo: un logro con límites

sections.content: Pese a que (despite the fact that) is another close relative of aunque and a pesar de que, and takes the subjunctive under the same rule -- ideal for a closing lesson that wants to honor a real achievement while immediately naming its real limits. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Pese a que resultara imposible imaginar, en 1930, un continente capaz de fabricar acero y automóviles, esa transformación se había convertido en una realidad consolidada hacia los años sesenta.
items.english: Despite it being impossible to imagine, in 1930, a continent capable of manufacturing steel and cars, that transformation had become a consolidated reality by the 1960s.

items.spanish: Pese a que este logro industrial resultara genuinamente impresionante, varios economistas señalaron problemas estructurales serios.
items.english: Despite this industrial achievement being genuinely impressive, several economists pointed to serious structural problems.

items.spanish: Pese a que la industrialización había transformado radicalmente ciudades como São Paulo, el desarrollo se concentró desproporcionadamente en unas pocas regiones.
items.english: Despite industrialization having radically transformed cities like São Paulo, development was concentrated disproportionately in a few regions.

items.spanish: Pese a que la industrialización latinoamericana representara un logro histórico genuino, las semillas de futuras dificultades ya estaban sembradas dentro de su propio éxito.
items.english: Despite Latin American industrialization representing a genuine historical achievement, the seeds of future difficulties were already sown within its own success.

sections.content: Pese a (without que) works directly before a noun -- pese a las dificultades -- exactly like a pesar de and debido a; the que version always introduces a full clause with its own conjugated verb.
